title: wait_for_task offers work that claim_next_task refuses to a block-holding worker
description: Filed by governor-7610ed5a from worker-0b2f9c35's measured report (#governors msg-3b0f1bdf, 03:49Z). MEASURED, twice in one session: a worker holding a BLOCKED task calls wait_for_task → hasNext:true naming a claimable CRITICAL task; then claim_next_task → hasNext:false with "alreadyAssigned: <blocked task> ... status BLOCKED". wait_for_task does not apply the claim-eligibility filter (caller already holds an assignment), so the prescribed wrapper loop (wait → claim on hasNext) spins indefinitely, and the two tools' nextAction hints contradict (claim says "end session and idle", report_blocked says "call wait_for_task"). FLEET HARM: claimable CRITICAL work sits in WORKING while the daemon repeatedly offers it to a worker it will refuse — a stall dressed as a busy queue; with several block-holding workers this generalizes. FIX SHAPE (architect decides): either wait_for_task applies the same eligibility predicate claim_next_task enforces (don't wake a worker for work it cannot take), or claim_next_task for a worker holding a BLOCKED task releases-and-claims / returns an actionable nextAction (e.g. "release your blocked assignment first" with the tool call), and the two nextAction hints are made consistent. Regression test: worker holds a BLOCKED task, a claimable task exists — assert wait_for_task and claim_next_task agree (both offer with a workable path, or both decline with the same reason).
definitionOfDone: A worker holding a BLOCKED task is never woken by wait_for_task for work that claim_next_task will refuse it — the two tools apply one eligibility predicate

The nextAction guidance across report_blocked, wait_for_task and claim_next_task forms a workable loop for a block-holding worker (no wait→claim→refuse spin, no contradictory end-session/keep-waiting pair)
A test with a real store covers the block-holding-worker scenario and is red before the fix

THE TWO SIDES, measured by the architect: (1) claimNextTask.ts:99-135 -- any worker holding an active task other than the requested one gets hasNext:false alreadyAssigned{...}; a BLOCKED hold (:109) additionally gets the 'Do NOT work on it. End your session' hint (:127). getActiveTasksAssignedToWorker evidently INCLUDES BLOCKED holds -- confirm by reading its definition in the state layer, because the whole bug reduces to wait_for_task not consulting this same source. (2) waitForTask.ts:202 -- `findMatchingTask(state, statuses, params.epicId, workerId)` answers the immediate path with hasNext:true and a nextAction that says CLAIM IT (:205-212), with no check of the CALLER'S holds; the waiter-wake path has the same gap. READ CAREFULLY before touching: the comment at :103-110 (a blocked worker's wait must wake when its own task's RESOURCE is granted) and :120 ('any task that is wait-visible but claim-ineligible wakes the waiter') -- the second comment documents a DELIBERATE broad-wake choice for OTHER workers' visibility, and the fix must narrow only the CALLER-holds-a-block case, not the general wake semantics. Also confirm the third guidance text in reportBlocked.ts (:158 region, 'call wait_for_task') -- DoD 2 requires all three tools' hints to form one workable loop.

MEASURED at D:/projexts/moes HEAD a0646b3.

(1) CLAIM SIDE — claimNextTask.ts:99-135 confirmed as the architect described. held = state.getActiveTasksAssignedToWorker(workerId).filter(t => t.id !== params.taskId); any remainder => hasNext:false + alreadyAssigned{taskId,title,status,+blockedReason/blockedResourceId when blocked}. blockedHold = current.status === 'BLOCKED' at :109. The BLOCKED nextAction (:120-128) points at moe.list_resources with reason "...Do NOT work on it. End your session and let the wrapper idle, or check the queue with list_resources." — list_resources is a dead end for a non-resource block. Non-blocked branch (:129-133) already names release_task.

(2) THE SOURCE — CONFIRMED, and the architect's "evidently" is now measured fact: workerStore.ts:34 ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES = Set(['PLANNING','WORKING','REVIEW','BLOCKED']) — BLOCKED IS in the set, with the in-file rationale at :31-33 ("a worker parked on a resource queue still owns its task"). getActiveTasksAssignedToWorker (workerStore.ts:85-87) filters on that set, reached via StateManager.ts:582-584. So a BLOCKED hold does come back from the same source claimNextTask uses; the :109 branch is live, not dead. NOTE, doc drift found and deliberately NOT fixed (out of granted scope): the JSDoc on that very function still says "(PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW)" — one status stale vs its own constant. Flagging, not touching.

(3) WAIT SIDE — waitForTask.ts:95-135 findMatchingTask(state, statuses, epicId, workerId). It DOES take workerId, and uses it for exactly two things: the own-task wake (:103-115) and the solo-worker-per-epic-status mirror (:132-135). It never asks whether the CALLER is encumbered. Immediate path :202-213 returns hasNext:true + nextAction moe.claim_next_task reason "Task is available; claim it, then call moe.get_context." The eligibility mirror at :123-135 covers state.isTaskClaimable, the needsHumanReview REVIEW park, and solo-worker — every ineligibility EXCEPT caller-holds-a-task. The file's own comment at :116-121 states the invariant it breaks verbatim: "any task that is wait-visible but claim-ineligible wakes the waiter into a claim that declines straight back to wait_for_task — a hot wake->claim->wait spin at full RPC speed for as long as the task persists." So this is a gap in an intent the file already declares, not a design disagreement.

TWO PRESERVES CONFIRMED IN-FILE: (a) own-task wake :103-110 comment "a worker parked on wait_for_task while its task sat BLOCKED must wake when the resource grant flips it back to WORKING"; (b) the broad-wake choice at :116-121 which serves OTHER workers' visibility. Fix narrows only the caller-encumbered case.

(4) REPORT SIDE — reportBlocked.ts:147-167. waitStatuses maps a human-gated status onto an agent-claimable one; nextAction is emitted only when task.assignedWorkerId && !params.resourceId, tool moe.wait_for_task, reason "Block reported; wait for human to unblock (via chat) or for a different task to pick up." That "or for a different task to pick up" clause is precisely the false promise — a block-holding worker can never pick up a different task. Resource-blocked case already correctly emits NO nextAction (:158-160 comment). So the hint region to change is the non-resource branch only.

(5) TEST GROUND — both test files exist with real-store fixtures. claimNextTask.test.ts (17.2KB) has alreadyAssigned coverage at :203 and :224. waitForTask.test.ts (8.2KB) already has the ideal home: describe 'wait_for_task eligibility mirrors claim_next_task (hot-loop regressions)' at :76 with mkdtemp + real StateManager + writeTask/writeWorker helpers and three sibling spin-regression cases. New cases go there.

(6) BASELINE GATE — package is `moe-daemon` (NOT scoped @moe/*), test script is `vitest run`. implementationPlan.description: RED. Extend waitForTask.test.ts and claimNextTask.test.ts with the DoD-3 regression over the real state store, red before the fix: SCENARIO -- worker W holds task A in BLOCKED; claimable task B (PLANNING, unassigned, matching statuses) exists. Assert: (1) wait_for_task for W does NOT return hasNext:true naming B (today it does -- red); instead it returns a response whose nextAction explains the blocked hold and the workable options (idle for the wrapper, or release_task to free the slot), consistent with what claim_next_task says; (2) claim_next_task for W still refuses with alreadyAssigned (existing behavior, keep green) but its blocked-hold nextAction now names the actionable pair -- `moe.release_task {taskId: A}` preserves the blockedReason and frees the worker to claim -- rather than only 'end your session'; (3) THE AGREEMENT PROPERTY, the test the DoD actually asks for: for the same (worker, board) state, wait_for_task's hasNext and claim_next_task's willingness agree -- assert it directly by driving both tools and comparing, not by duplicating each tool's logic in the test; (4) PRESERVED WAKES: W's wait still wakes when task A's blockedResourceId lease is granted (the :103-110 path), and a DIFFERENT unencumbered worker W2 still gets hasNext:true for B immediately -- the fix must not dim the queue for eligible workers.
implementationPlan.note:
RED achieved on the real store — 4 new tests, all failing for the intended reason, 20 pre-existing green. No production byte touched yet.

RUN: `npx vitest run src/tools/waitForTask.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts` from packages/moe-daemon, EXIT=1 (PIPESTATUS[0], not the grep's). Count line: "Tests 4 failed | 20 passed (24)", "Test Files 2 failed (2)".

THE FOUR FAILURES AND WHY EACH IS THE RIGHT RED:
1. claimNextTask.test.ts:279 'a BLOCKED hold refuses the claim and names release_task as the actionable exit' — AssertionError: expected 'moe.list_resources' to be 'moe.release_task'. That IS the dead-end hint measured in step 1 (claimNextTask.ts:121). alreadyAssigned assertions already pass, so this test pins ONLY the guidance defect and keeps the load-bearing refusal shape green.
2. claimNextTask.test.ts:305 'wait_for_task and claim_next_task give a block-holding worker the SAME answer' — expected true to be false on waitResult.hasNext. This is the measured spin reproduced in a test: wait offers, claim refuses.
3. waitForTask.test.ts:247 'does NOT offer foreign work to a worker holding a BLOCKED task' — expected true to be false, same false offer from the wait side alone.
4. waitForTask.test.ts:282 'still PARKS a resource-blocked holder and wakes it when its own task is granted' — expected false to be true on activeWaiters.has('worker-w'). Today the resource-blocked holder never parks because it is answered immediately with a foreign offer. This is a PRESERVE test that is currently red for the same root cause; it is the assertion that stops me from "fixing" the spin by returning an immediate refusal to everyone, which would silently delete the resource-grant wake.

DESIGN DECISION FORCED BY TEST 4, and it changes the fix shape the plan sketched — recording it because a reader of the plan will otherwise expect a single unconditional early return. waitForTask.ts:103-115 wakes a waiter on its OWN task, but only when that task is in a REQUESTED status. Statuses are restricted to PLANNING/WORKING/REVIEW (assertAgentClaimableStatuses), so a BLOCKED hold can NEVER match the own-task path — which is exactly why the BLOCKED hold is the one active status where wait and claim could drift, and why no other hold produced this bug. It also means an unconditional immediate refusal for every blocking hold would destroy the documented resource-grant wake (:103-110). So the narrowing is two-branch: a hold WITHOUT an auto-unblock path answers immediately with the shared refusal; a hold WITH blockedResourceId still PARKS (its grant is precisely what the waiter exists to catch) and merely has foreign offers suppressed. Both branches satisfy the single property that matters — wait never offers what claim refuses.

AGREEMENT PROPERTY, built as the DoD asks: test 2 drives BOTH production tools against one board and compares their actual answers — expect(waitResult.alreadyAssigned).toEqual(claimResult.alreadyAssigned) and expect(waitResult.nextAction).toEqual(claimResult.nextAction). No copy of either predicate exists in the test, so the step-4 drill can genuinely break it.

NON-VACUITY, deliberately built in because a suite that stops offering work to everyone would pass a naive version of all four: every refusal test carries a POSITIVE CONTROL on the same board — the same task-free is asserted still wait-visible AND still claimable for an unencumbered second worker (worker-free in waitForTask.test.ts, w-2 in claimNextTask.test.ts, both tools driven).

FILES: waitForTask.test.ts 226->291 lines (LF preserved), claimNextTask.test.ts 415->488 lines (CRLF preserved, plus one import of activeWaiters/waitForTaskTool). Line endings were mixed across the six granted paths and were checked per file before writing. Test files only; the 250/400 cap is a per-production-file rail.

DESIGN CHANGED MID-STEP, and this is the part a reviewer should read. I first wrote the immediate refusal the plan sketched (return heldTaskRefusal as soon as an encumbered caller has nothing to claim). Then the sibling task's commit f5c5079 landed on reportBlocked.ts while I worked — "resolve the repeat's wait hint from the restore target" — and reading it changed my mind. Their fix makes report_blocked hint the RESTORE status rather than BLOCKED, so a blocked worker's wait actually matches its own task when the unblock lands. That is not a rival fix, it is the other half of mine: parking a blocked worker is how it catches its own unblock (resource grant OR moe.unblock_worker), and my immediate return would have silently deleted that wake for every non-resource block. So I reverted the early return. Final shape: the caller still PARKS, only the foreign OFFER is suppressed, and the TIMEOUT answer carries the shared refusal payload (alreadyAssigned + release_task hint) instead of the bare "re-enter wait to keep listening". Same DoD, no behaviour destroyed, and no branch on blockedResourceId needed at all — the design got simpler by being forced to respect a peer's work.

Their identicalRepeat "NOTHING was recorded" clause is preserved verbatim.

THE THREE HINTS NOW AGREE: claim_next_task -> release_task or idle; wait_for_task (timeout) -> the identical object, from the identical builder; report_blocked -> park for your own unblock, or release_task. No tool tells a block-holding worker it can pick up other work, and none tells it to end the session while another tells it to keep waiting.

comments.content:
REPRODUCTION DATA from architect-77071474, hit three times in one session on 2026-08-17/18. Not a report of the symptom — a narrowing of it, with the discriminating experiment.

**OBSERVATION 1 — the refusal message is wrong about the cause.**
`moe.claim_next_task {statuses:["PLANNING"], workerId:"architect-77071474"}` returned:
```
hasNext: false
reason: "All candidate tasks were taken by concurrent workers; wait and retry."
```
At that same moment a direct read of `.moe/tasks/*.json` showed **10 PLANNING tasks with `assignedWorkerId: null`**. Nothing had been taken. The message names a race that was not happening.

**OBSERVATION 2 — the refusal is not per-task.**
Claiming one of those unassigned tasks BY EXPLICIT `taskId` returned the same `hasNext: false`. So it is not ranking, not filtering, and not that particular task.

**OBSERVATION 3 — the discriminator.** The identical explicit call, with only `replaceExisting: true` added, **succeeded immediately**:
```
claim_next_task {statuses:["PLANNING"], taskId:"task-4731ba34...", replaceExisting:true}
-> hasNext: true, assignedWorkerId: "architect-77071474"
```
Nothing about the target changed between those two calls. Only the flag did.

**DIAGNOSIS:** the refusal is about the CALLER's state, not the candidate's. `replaceExisting` is documented as "replace existing worker assignment if another worker is active" — i.e. a fact about the TARGET — but it is behaving as the gate on the caller already holding an assignment. The generic "taken by concurrent workers" message is then emitted for a condition that has nothing to do with concurrency, which is what makes this so hard to diagnose from the message alone.

**CORROBORATING CASE, and it may be the more serious one:** earlier in the same session I held task-e62e3828 in **BLOCKED** status. `claim_next_task` refused with a different and more accurate response — it named the held task and said "You hold task-… but it is BLOCKED. Do NOT work on it. End your session and let the wrapper idle." Calling `moe.release_task` on the blocked task freed the slot and the next claim worked. So a BLOCKED holding is detected and explained correctly, while a *stale or completed* holding appears to fall through to the misleading concurrency message. That asymmetry is a good place to look.

**WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ANNOYANCE:** `wait_for_task` is the documented `nextAction` after this refusal. A worker that follows the runtime's own guidance parks waiting for work that is sitting unassigned on the board — the exact stall in this task's title. It also interacts badly with `mem:empty-worker-queue-can-mean-dead-architect`: an architect seeing an empty queue may conclude the board is drained when it is not.

**SUGGESTED ACCEPTANCE SHAPE** (offered, not prescribed — the owning architect should measure first): the refusal must name which condition fired, and a caller holding nothing must never receive the concurrency message while unassigned candidates exist. A test that seeds N unassigned PLANNING tasks, calls `claim_next_task` from a worker holding nothing, and asserts a claim rather than `hasNext:false` would have caught this; assert the returned `taskId` is one of the seeded ids, not merely that `hasNext` is true.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The description offers two fix shapes; DoD 1's wording ('the two tools apply one eligibility predicate', 'never woken for work claim will refuse') settles it as the shared-predicate design, so the real decisions were narrower. (1) WHAT THE BLOCK-HOLDING WAITER GETS instead of a false offer: hasNext:false plus guidance naming BOTH workable exits -- wrapper idle (the designed path: BLOCKED suppresses relaunch, resource grants auto-unblock) and release_task (the path every blocked-then-sweeping worker on this board has used, preserving blockedReason; measured by this architect a dozen times this session). Chose to present both rather than pick one because the right exit depends on whether the session is wrapper-driven or interactive, which the daemon cannot see. (2) RELEASE-AND-CLAIM AUTOMATICALLY inside claim_next_task -- rejected: releasing a hold is a state-visible act with a handoff-note contract; doing it implicitly inside a claim would silently drop the correction-note opportunity and surprise the wrapper's alreadyAssigned-keyed suppression. The hint NAMES the release; the worker performs it deliberately. (3) Where the predicate lives: beside claimableStatuses.ts in the existing util layer, built on getActiveTasksAssignedToWorker -- the same source claimNextTask uses today -- so there is exactly one definition of 'this worker is encumbered'; the drill simulates predicate drift and requires the agreement test to catch it, because the agreement PROPERTY (drive both tools, compare answers) is the only test shape that stays valid if either tool's internals change. (4) reportBlocked's hint is in scope because DoD 2 names the three-tool loop: today report_blocked says 'call wait_for_task', wait offers refused work, claim says 'end session' -- the spin is the three texts composed; aligning only two would leave the entry edge broken.

planningNotes.risks: The subtle risk is over-narrowing the wake semantics: waitForTask's broad wake (:120) exists so a waiter learns the pool changed even when a specific task is claim-ineligible FOR OTHERS' reasons -- if the fix filters ALL ineligibility instead of only the caller's own blocking hold, workers stop waking for contested-but-releasable work and the queue dims fleet-wide; the preserved-wake assertions in step 2 (W2 still offered B; W still woken by its own resource grant) pin the boundary.
